body:
If possible, would like to include https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11839 in the agenda to talk about two pending concerns about focus-without-user-activation policy:

a) interaction with **fullscreen** (brought up by @smaug----). Proposing to add an extra `if` statement in the `allow focus steps` to avoid focus to be programmatically moved outside of frames with fullscreen on. https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11519#issuecomment-3676484450

b) behaviors of **popups** (brought up by @annevk). Proposing to treat them in the same way iframes are treated in the issue's proposal: allow subframes (or popup descendants) to manage focus once they have focus.
Expanded in this comment https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11519#discussion_r2636495114. Also made a table to try and exhaust all possible cases:
Focused document | Caller document | Target document | Focus call is allowed
-- | -- | -- | --
A | A | A | Yes
A | A | B | Yes
B | A | A | Yes
B | A | B | Yes
A | B | A | No
A | B | B | No
B | B | A | Yes
B | B | B | Yes

Thanks!

Earlier today we held this meeting, minutes are below.  The next meeting will be on 2026-01-22 in the APAC-EMEA-friendly timezone: https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12087.
 
- **Review of Previous Agenda+ Items** Chris Wilson addressed existing agenda items. Jacques Newman confirmed that [11641](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11641) (declarative keyboard focus navigation) could be removed unless there was anything new, and they didn't think there was. Kurt Catti-Schmidt advised that item #[11981](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11981) (allow style and JSON in an attribute for modulepreload) could be removed from the agenda, as Anne had given a plus one, and they planned to land it on Tuesday, acknowledging Monday was a holiday.
- **Focused Behavior with Subframes and Denied Policy** Fernando Fiori provided a check-in on [11839](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11839) (focused behavior with subframes and denied policy), stating they had addressed comments regarding focus without user activation policy. Olli Pettay mentioned that they couldn't review the latest changes due to GitHub being down, but discussed the use of the incumbent global object over the entry global object for this case, which Fernando Fiori agreed to investigate.
- **Toggle Events for Select Elements** #[11564](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11564) A discussion was held regarding adding `toggle` and `beforetoggle` events for customizable selects, similar to popovers. Luke raised potential complexities with `appearance: auto` and ensuring compatibility, especially concerning multiple selects with a size of one, which can display differently across browsers. Olli Pettay expressed concern that relying on these new events, particularly in cases where pop-up behavior varies by browser (like with multiple selects), could lead to web compatibility issues. Emilio Cobos Álvarez suggested it would be weird to fire the events conditionally based on appearance, as it could change mid-event, but thought firing them based on the existence of a pop-up was fine, though acknowledged the issue of interop with the multiple size one case. Luke noted that deferring the implementation until there is more interop might be necessary, but this would be complicated by the difficulty of feature detecting the events. Someone in The Wizard Of Oz (us-sfo-fre215) later confirmed they would summarize Emilio Cobos Álvarez's idea in the GitHub thread.
- **Updating Mutation Observer API** https://github.com/whatwg/dom/issues/1439  Olli Pettay proposed a generic update for the Mutation Observer API, which was designed 15 years ago before features like Shadow DOM. They noted that a holistic update would be better than small, one-by-one tweaks, and the effort for implementation was expected to be low. Lea Verou and sideshowbarker agreed, with Lea Verou noting that current workarounds for API deficiencies are often slow, and sideshowbarker highlighting the high value for web developers if the implementation effort is low. Lea Verou raised the importance of consistent API shape for observing Shadow Roots across various DOM methods. Olli Pettay plans to create a document to gather ideas and discuss potential changes, including how to handle concepts like disconnect handling and if these should extend to other observer APIs.
- **Out of Order Streaming Proposal** https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11542 Noam Rosenthal introduced a new proposal for out of order streaming, which replaces the start and end markers with a single new `marker` node. The template would replace content between the first and last markers, or all children if no marker is present, or just the single marker if only one exists, simplifying the process for appending and prepending content. This marker would be a new immutable void node type, but Noam Rosenthal noted they could consider a processing instruction if adding a new node type was problematic for compatibility. Jake Archibald and Lea Verou questioned the nature of the new marker node, including its single form for starting and ending a range, and potential parallels to slots. Noam Rosenthal clarified that using a single marker type simplifies append and prepend operations, and while the first proposal involved a slot element, this new approach aims for a non-nested parser directive specifically for out-of-order streaming, acting like a "one time slot". The markers must be direct children of the sync element when the template is discovered by the parser, and their association is maintained as a live range afterward. For next steps, Noam Rosenthal will update the explainer document and may discuss the proposal further on Matrix before deciding if it should be an agenda item for the following week.
